messages:
incident-bot: PAGER DUTY — elevated p99 latency observed for streaming endpoints in eu-west-2. Metric alert: streaming.p99 > 1.5s over 5m (current p99=4.8s, p95=1.2s). Increased streaming stalls & tail latency. Affected routes: /v1/stream (ws), /v1/chat/stream. Runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/incidents/streaming-latency-eu. Page sent to @Carla M. :rotating_light:

Carla M.: Acked — I’m oncall for infra. starting quick triage. grabbing dashboard + netflow.

Carla M.: quick snapshot: 5m window shows cross-AZ egress retransmits up ~8x for eu-west-2a->nat. streaming stalls metric spiked (stalls_pct 9% -> 38%). No errors from model cluster itself (cpu/gpu normal).

Ben K.: pinging in — neteng. can you drop a traceroute from a problem pod to external endpoint?

Carla M.: running tcpdump on a proxy in eu-west-2a and a pod in eu-west-2b now.

Carla M.: traceroute output (trimmed):
```
traceroute to 1.2.3.4 (1.2.3.4), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.1.1 (10.0.1.1)  0.32 ms  0.28 ms  0.26 ms
 2  100.64.0.1 (100.64.0.1)  1.2 ms  1.3 ms  1.4 ms
 3  52.95.0.1 (52.95.0.1)  45.1 ms  44.9 ms  44.8 ms  <-- jitter
 4  * * *
```

Carla M.: tcpdump shows repeated retransmits and some connection resets on TLS handshake during tail windows.

Ben K.: likely NAT gateway or cross-AZ routing flap. I'm checking NAT gateway metrics and ENI quotas.

infra-bot: ALERT: NAT gateway active flows spiked to 4.2k (baseline 800). Pixel: nat-gw-eu-2-1 nearing ephemeral port exhaustion.

Ben K.: that aligns. ephemeral port exhaustion would cause new TLS handshakes to fail or stall -> streaming handshakes time out causing stalls.

Dan S.: @Carla @Ben recommend immediate mitigation steps from runbook: 1) shift a portion of traffic to eu-west-1 (steer at edge), 2) expand NAT capacity or attach an additional NAT, 3) adjust NLB connection draining/idle settings to avoid burst teardown. Which should we do first?

Carla M.: I can spin up an extra NAT GW in eu-west-2 and attach to private subnets — ETA ~3-4m. I’ll also temporarily set edge routing policy to send 30% of streaming traffic to eu-west-1 for warm failover.

Ben K.: I'll request quota bump for new ENI if needed and pre-attach NAT. If we add NAT it should reduce port pressure immediately. Also enabling source/destination check toggles for specific proxies if needed.

Carla M.: executing:
```
# create nat gw and attach to private subnet
aws ec2 allocate-address --domain vpc --query AllocationId
aws ec2 create-nat-gateway --subnet-id subnet-xxxx --allocation-id eipalloc-xxxx
aws ec2 create-route-table --vpc-id vpc-xxxx
# (omitted manual steps)
```

Carla M.: NAT GW created and in pending -> available. Edge rule change queued: steering 30% to eu-west-1.

Emma L. (support): FYI customers reporting streaming rebuffering. Triage note: 4 customers with active sessions reported pauses >=10s, no aborts. We're sending status to affected customers in EU region.

Carla M.: after NAT up, initial metrics show active flows spread across two NATs, ephemeral port usage dropping. p99 trending down from 4.8s -> 2.1s in first 2m. stalls_pct down 38% -> 18%.

Ben K.: confirming route table entries look good. No ENI quota errors now. Still see some packet loss on one AZ path (eu-west-2c -> nat-gw-1). I'm going to route around that AZ for a short window.

Carla M.: switching autoscaler to avoid placing new proxy pods in eu-west-2c for 15m.

Dan S.: Good. Please add a short customer impact summary for PS and AE teams: how many sessions affected, duration, and mitigation. Emma can you draft?

Emma L. (support): Drafting now: 1) Impact window: 03/24 14:04 - ongoing mitigation at 14:20, reduction in impact 14:24, normalizing ~14:35. 2) ~1200 streaming sessions in eu-west-2, estimated 0.3% experienced stalls >=5s, 4 customers reported visible interruption. 3) Root cause suspected NAT ephemeral port exhaustion combined with intermittent cross-AZ routing packet loss. Mitigation: spin up additional NAT GW, steer 30% traffic to eu-west-1, avoid problematic AZ.

Carla M.: Last check: p95=1.1s, p99=0.95s (below SLO) — marking incident as mitigated. We should keep monitoring for 30m.

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by Carla M. Resolved? Please update status when postmortem assigned.

Ben K.: filing a follow-up ticket to investigate NAT scaling behavior and any cloud provider network events impacting AZ paths. I'll tag neteng and cloudops.

Dan S.: actions for postmortem: 1) Confirm root cause: port exhaustion vs provider packet loss correlation with cloud provider events, 2) Review NAT architecture: add autoscaling or use managed NAT pool per AZ, 3) Improve alerting threshold to detect port exhaustion earlier, 4) Update runbook with explicit edge-steering playbook.

Carla M.: I'll take owner for immediate runbook updates and short RCA draft. Ben you own long-term NAT design changes. Dan you'll run postmortem and severity classification.

Carla M.: closing thread for active paging — continuing monitoring in #eng-sre for 30m. Thanks all :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: mitigated — human remediation performed (NAT added, traffic steering). Please attach logs and metric snapshots to the postmortem ticket.
